dedupe_keys.name: inland navigation waterways and infrastructure of the congo basin cicos

description: Two pages of the CICOS site describe the navigable waterways and the inland navigation infrastructure of the Congo basin. The waterways page states a navigable network of at least 17,000 kilometres according to the CICOS database, explains the seasonal high and low water periods of the Ubangi, Lobaye, Sangha, N'Goko and Congo rivers, and notes that river transport has declined since the 1990s because of old and insufficient infrastructure, poor maintenance, weak regulation and non-physical barriers. The infrastructure page gives a country-by-country inventory in text and maps: for Cameroon, ten developed landing points such as Socambo with its 110 and 160 tonne ferries; for the Central African Republic, the ports of Bangui (28,000 square metres, three quays, about thirty warehouses and ten cranes) and the Kolongo oil port with about 50,000 cubic metres of storage, plus 18 landing points with commercial status; and for the Republic of Congo, the port of Brazzaville, four secondary river ports and six landing points. Access is free and public on the web pages; no licence is stated. Caveats: the pages are narrative inventories from about 2015, not datasets, and they are in French. Coverage is the Congo basin. It supports network and capacity planning of inland waterway transport and exposure of river ports to low water; the related record is the CICOS hydrological information system.
